description: Technical lead on rapid AI prototyping for enterprise clients. Built generative AI features for a major financial client — a RAG-based conversational interface and dynamic UI generation from data analysis. Also engineered an AI exam-marker for an eLearning company that outperformed human accuracy. Mostly serverless Python and .NET on AWS, plus a full React/Vite rebuild of a business-critical multilingual app along the way.

Loved this project — working in such a large organisation on a transformation piece is always a challenge, and throwing multiple brands into the mix made it more interesting. A chance to build not just a UI framework, but a customer-centred design philosophy from the ground up for one of Australia's biggest banks.

REST wanted to lift member engagement. Completely greenfield setup using serverless, event-driven architecture with lots of integration. I love starting a new project where I get a say in how it should be designed and built — very satisfying. REST is a great company too, awesome people and a truly great business to work for.

Built a complete backend that let users of the REST app search, combine and rollover their super. Created services around KYC, MFA, OTP and a bunch of others. I got to work mostly on the security side which I enjoyed immensely.

An unlikely candidate for a design system. As part of a team I led the direction, creation and implementation of this piece of work. The guide has a nice cross-section of components to choose from — and takes it further with block-level implementations.

Built prototypes for the St.George banking mobile app, the St.George tablet app, and the Westpac payments app. Focused on micro-interactions and the user experience — the end result was some really nice apps.
A few years working with Macquarie Bank on a long list of applications — too many to list. This particular one was for one of the Korean infrastructure funds.

A great company to work for. Hired to help build a new business — exciting from day one. My first React project (and they still hired me). We built a small component library and a completely serverless business in three months. The ROI on this was massive.
amaysim selling iPhones. Our team was mostly responsible for the UI side. Lots of GraphQL and React.
Mostly UI work for this one. A nice vibrant colour scheme — refer a friend, get a credit on your account, your friend gets one too.
My first government role. Led a team on an Angular project to build an application to manage significant events. Initially for NSW Police — it's now used by multiple agencies.
Content management system, online store, Google Maps integration. Launched at Christmas, also the 50th anniversary of Barbie. The site was getting a million users a month and hardly broke a sweat.
Interesting project — the first multilingual build I'd done in ages.
One of NRMA's first online forms — a massive new-platform build. Among the earliest projects in the company to emphasise UX, with customer testing and a fresh UI.

Joined as AMP started using Angular 2 in beta — a brave call at the time. By the time we shipped, the framework had matured and several apps were live in production. Components were mostly stateful, sometimes with their own services. A great engineering team and clear product ownership made the early bet pay off.
Macquarie Radio Network's bid to compete with News Limited and Fairfax. Hundreds of thousands of users daily, live feeds, ads, weather — the full online news stack. My first lead role.
The Perpetual Investments website — one of the first industrial-strength web applications I had the pleasure of working on. Early experience shipping into a regulated financial environment.
A small e-commerce site I built a very long time ago. The business has since been sold and has a new look and feel.
A small e-commerce build for selling irrigation equipment, and one of my last .NET projects before moving fully to modern web. The business has since wound up.
Long-running personal side project — domain purchased years ago, evolving as a blog, app, and whatever comes next.
